text:
sam: quick follow-up on the canary/fallback patterns. proposing a hybrid approach: content-aware trimming in the router + optional proxy stripper as a last-resort. want a compact operator story and low-cardinality telemetry.

marta: short questions: 1) when does router trim vs send to proxy? 2) how do we measure semantic impact without leaking text?

sam: router-first: apply thinning levels (0..3) inline for stateless requests. proxy-relay only used when memory pressure is extreme or trimming not effective. trimming is guided by per-segment salience scores.

lee: for telemetry we can emit a tiny equivalence token: sha256(prefix_kept)[:8] + kept_len, sampled at 0.02%. reservoir-sample to bound cardinality. rollups only.

raj: ops concern: private/dedicated customers may not want router plugins. how to support them?

nina: provide two modes: router-plugin for hosted, client-side library or sidecar for private. both honor the same X-Deg header contract so controllers interoperate.

marta: fallback triggers? we need to avoid flip-flop between thinning levels or proxy.

sam: propose a two-axis rule: quick trigger (latency or error spike) escalates to next thinning level; persistent breach (>=3m) escalates to proxy-mode. de-escalation needs a stable-window of 10m. also require mirror validation before enabling a new level beyond 1%.

lee: add sentinel checks: sample N prompts through full vs trimmed path and compute top-token agreement; if agreement < threshold -> block escalation. sample only on anonymized hashes.

raj: config sketch for operator UI (single-line JSON in header and admin flags):

X-Deg-Policy: {"mirror_pct":"5","levels":"[0,1,2,3]","start_level":0,"sample_pct":"0.02","fallback_rule":"two_axis"}

nina: rollout plan: 1) mirror-only 5% to trimming plugin (no trim) for 30m, 2) enable level=1 for 1% with circuit breaker, 3) monitor drift and latency 4) if sustained, level up gradually, 5) proxy-mode as emergency path.

ops-bot: canary job created: canary/deg-hybrid/mirror -> staging (id: 99211).

marta: sounds pragmatic. sam can you add a short RFC section with router pseudocode, header contract, and operator checklist? I'll review.

sam: on it. will include pseudocode and the sampling/reservoir guidance. tagging @lee @raj for quick review. :thumbsup:
